blindSummary:
This is a self-governing overseas territory of a distant administering state, and the law that applies here — marriage, legal gender recognition, penal-code anti-discrimination provisions — is inherited directly from that state's civil-law system. The territory's main city has a small visible trans scene.

Local deviations from the administering state's baseline are modest: somewhat stronger local conservatism, and political unrest in 2024.
blindOutOfScope: Dependency status is general governance context, not trans-specific risk; deviations noted in the summary.
blindSourceSummaries: News outlet feature (Jan 2018, metropolitan context): trans women in the administering state incarcerated on the basis of their legal gender fall into a legal gray area - relevant to this territory because it applies the administering state's law.

The administering state's national detention-watchdog opinion of 25 May 2021 on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty (metropolitan law, applicable in this territory): serious violations persist across places of detention.
A cable-news report (May 2013): the administering state's first same-sex wedding after its marriage-equality law; that law applies in this territory.

LGBT news outlet (Aug 2012): the administering state's same-sex marriage bill (marriage and adoption) to be introduced in October, fulfilling the sitting head of state's campaign pledge - the legislation that extended marriage equality to this territory as metropolitan law.

The administering state's lower-house parliamentary session record (2016-17): proceedings relevant to overseas territories including this one - the metropolitan legislative framework that applies (page largely navigation content at fetch time).

LGBT news site covering the administering state (July 2012): 'sexual identity' became a discrimination ground in the penal code via the sexual-harassment law - enabling prosecution of transphobia as discrimination; that law applies in this territory.
